note: Digging with the shovel (docs/future/13 section 10, P2c; src/world/dig). Tune with tools/dig-lab.html. hole: a hole's size (m across), the dig point ahead of the walker (aheadM), the least gap between open holes (spacingM: a press nearer an open hole than this digs that hole deeper), how far a hole may slide off a plant's stem (slideM, tried in slideSteps rings of 8 directions) and how far it keeps clear of a placed piece's footprint (pieceClearM); plantClearM is how near a plant's middle a hole may come. ground: ankleM, the deepest water (live, or the habitat's standing fresh water) a hole may be dug in; dampBank, the moisture (0..1, at least) and salt (at most) that make grass, soil or moss ground a damp bank, where clay lies a spade down. layers: the stack under each ground class, top first, and the word said at the bottom (stones, harder: a deeper layer the shovel cannot reach yet, sand). fill: a hole fills a third of the way each hoursPerThird game hours, each hour of rain counting rainWeight times, in four stages (open, slumped, settled, closed); a closed hole's darker patch fades over darkDays; at most openCap holes are open (a new one beyond settles the oldest closed at once) and the list keeps at most listCap records; waterM: live water this deep over a hole (a tide, a flood) closes it. rest: a cellM cell gives each layer once a game day; thin: in a patchM patch, the n-th dig of the season gives keepsakes at this share ([from the n-th, share]); it recovers at the season's turn. budget: the island's dug keepsakes a game day, 0, 1 or 2 with these weights, drawn from the seed. keepsake: the chance a dig holds one by layer, the family by layer, summerSandLean (drift seeds lean in in summer), holedLean (a dug stone's holed mark, at this share of the shore's). rarity: weights per layer depth (common, uncommon, rare, very rare, once in a lifetime); gates (a rare one needs depth 2, sand excepted; very rare and once in a lifetime need depth 3, which the first shovel never reaches); lean on rain yesterday and on a frost day (a winter day that dawned clear or misty). worms: the chance by layer and season (spring, summer, autumn, winter), summer times summerRainBoost after rain yesterday. clay: the seasons it can be worked. seep: a dig to a clay layer at least moistureMin wet shows water creeping into the hole until it slumps. startleM: a dig is an edit at the hole for presence within this reach. events.cap: the dug events kept this season. shovel: the test link that puts the shovel in the walker's kit (until the workbench makes it). act: the dig motion's sound beats (seconds into figure.json poses.dig): bite at the step, lift, pour as it tips; the hole changes at holeAtS and the card opens at cardAtS. look: the hole and spoil drawn (linear albedo by layer, the spoil heap's size and its shrinking by stage, the dark mouth's darkness and the fresh soil's darkening ring). scoop: Scoop sand on the here-bar, kneeling for kneelS; needs is the unlock it waits for. words: every line digging says; layers are the walker's first lines (drafts, docs/future/13 10.4.3); seen is a layer in words for the card and the shelf.

words.sand: Only sand below, and more sand.
words.harder: Something harder below. The shovel won't reach it.
words.clayWinter: Too stiff and cold to work. In spring.
words.thinned: This ground has given what it had this season. Somewhere else, perhaps.

layers.topsoil: Dark and crumbly, and threaded with roots. Everything here stands on this.
layers.subsoil: Paler underneath, and full of small stones. The roots thin out here.
layers.clay: Blue-grey, and it holds the spade. Clay. The pot is in here somewhere.
layers.sand: Clean sand, and cooler a hand down. The sea built this part.
layers.stones: Stones, and more stones under them. That's as deep as it goes here.
layers.seep: Water is creeping in from the sides. The ground is full of it here.

seen.subsoil: Pale brown subsoil, two spades down.
seen.sand: Clean pale sand, a spade down.

worm.small: A small red worm, quick as anything.
worm.big: A big dark worm, long as your hand.

words.clay1: A handful of clay, cool and sticky, into the pack.
words.covered: You set it back and cover it.
